  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Apply the Tukey-Kramer method for ANOVA-based pairwise comparisons to control the Family-Wise Error Rate (FWER). For non-parametric tests (Kruskal-Wallis/Dunn's), apply the Bonferroni correction to the p-values of the pairwise tests to maintain FWER control.",

    "Linearity and link function appropriateness for the binary 'Success' variable in the logistic model.",
    "Absence of extreme outliers in the continuous variables, particularly given the large max/min ratios observed in the summary statistics."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "The 'Combined' paradigm likely shows superior performance (lower Time-to-Target, higher Success, higher Path Efficiency, higher Average Speed, lower AD) compared to 'Sham' and single-modality paradigms, suggesting multimodal integration benefits.",
    "The 'ICMS Only' and visual-only paradigms may show intermediate performance, with 'Dim Visual Only' potentially performing worse than 'Bright Visual Only' due to reduced visual contrast.",
    "The 'Sham' group is expected to show the poorest performance metrics across the board, serving as the baseline control.",
    "Significant main effects are expected for all five response variables, with the magnitude of effect likely being largest for 'Success' and 'Time-to-Target'.",
    "Potential interactions between 'Mouse' ID and 'Stim Paradigm' if the data is nested (same mouse tested under multiple paradigms), which would require a mixed-effects analysis rather than a fixed-effects ANOVA."
  ],
  "limitations": [

    "The 'Success' variable is binary, making standard ANOVA assumptions (normality) technically invalid, requiring either transformation or a GLM approach.",
    "The sample size per group is unequal (Combined: 48846 vs Sham: 3505), which can affect the power and validity of post-hoc tests if variances are also unequal.",
    "No information is provided on the distribution of the data within groups, so assumption checking must be performed on the raw data, not just the summary statistics."
  ],

If data is nested by 'Mouse', refit the models as Linear Mixed-Effects Models (LMM) or Generalized Linear Mixed-Effects Models (GLMM) with 'Mouse' as a random effect.
